title: Balancing Image Compression and Generation with Bootstrapped Tokenization
claim: Prior tokenizers either mix all information in each token or inject local details inefficiently; ours decomposes and self-bootstraps to be efficient on every axis.
layout: 3 stacked panels (a)-(c), left-to-right flow, right-side smiley/frowny efficiency scorecard
description: Three horizontally stacked panels compare image tokenization designs: (a) original 1D tokenization, (b) 1D tokenization with global-local decomposition, and (c) the proposed self-bootstrapped version. Each panel shows a bird photo going through an Image Encoder (grey trapezoid) into a column of peach-colored tokens. The tokens go through a decoder or 'Decoding process' box and produce a reconstructed bird photo. Black arrows mark compression and red arrows mark generation, and a red 'Generator' box feeds the tokens. Panels (b) and (c) add white or grey local-token blocks and 'local info inject' arrows. Panel (c) adds 'local 1D' and 'local 2D' branches. At the right of each panel, three rows (Representation, Generation, Scaling Efficient) have red frowny or green smiley faces. Panel (a) has all frowns, (b) has one smiley, and (c) has all smileys. The eye goes first to the grey panels and the smiley column.
caption: Illustration of our self-bootstrapped learning paradigm. Compared to classical 1D image tokenizers [ref] and recent approaches incorporating local detail injection [ref], our method employs a global-local decomposition to achieve efficient hierarchical representation learning and adopts a self-bootstrapped strategy to enable both efficient generation and scalable training.
abstract: Despite progress in image tokenization, standard methods encode redundant information by mixing all granularities within each token, thus redundancy persists between tokens. The mix of information of different granularity also complicates the training of generators. This paper introduces SelfBootTok, a method that resolves this by cleanly decomposing information into global and local token groups. Through self-bootstrapped learning, the model predicts local details exclusively from global tokens, shifting the burden of visual details from the generator to the tokenizer. Consequently, our generator is far more efficient, requiring only global tokens and reducing computation by approximately 40%, while delivering superior reconstruction and generation. Moreover, this paradigm scales elegantly: by leveraging more data or parameters to self-supervise local representation learning, SelfBootTok achieves a new state-of-the-art gFID score of 1.56 using only 64 tokens.
